title: Convo Trimmer — lightweight context pruning (scratch)
content:
Goal / thesis:
- Make a cheap, low-risk way to reduce per-request token cost and KV cache bloat by automatically trimming low-value conversation history before sending to model.
- Target interactive chat flows where users accumulate long, repetitive context (multi-turn assistants, ticket triage, internal notebots).
- Keep UX predictable: no surprise deletions, reversible, and explainable.

Primary user problems we're solving:
- Token cost and latency increase with long visible history for each request.
- KV cache fill on the serving runtime can cause memory churn and evictions on long sessions.
- Product teams want a knob to trade a bit of context retention for cost without engineering complex heuristics in-app.

Non-goals
- Not a full summarization replacement.
- Not intended to change user-visible persona or facts (we should not delete critical user identity or ongoing task state).

Rough feature idea (high level)
- "Convo Trimmer" is a pre-send filter executed in the API/edge layer that marks and removes low-salience messages from the visible context payload.
- Configurable modes per-route or per-customer: aggressive, conservative, and seed-only. Default conservative.
- Simple heuristics + cheap classifier: age, redundancy (near-duplicate), role/system vs user/assistant, token length, and lightweight intent-change detection.
- Provide a delta (which messages were removed / why) in the response metadata for debugging and audit.

Basic flow
1) Client sends chat payload.
2) Trimmer runs over conversation history (window size configurable).
3) It returns a trimmed context + metadata (removed_ids[], reasons[]).
4) Backend continues normal inference with trimmed context.
5) Console/Logs show trimming decision and cost savings estimate.

User stories
- As a PM, I want a per-route toggle so I can enable trimming on low-risk assistants (FAQ bots) but keep full history for tasks that need long context.
- As an SRE, I want trimming to reduce average token-per-request so peak memory usage is more stable.
- As a developer, I want an easy flag in the SDK to preview trimming decisions so I can iterate prompts without surprises.
- As a customer admin, I want an audit log of what was removed for compliance (ability to disable trimming for regulated users).

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Conservative mode reduces tokens by >= 10% on 50% of sampled chats in internal benchmark dataset, with end-user quality delta <= 2% on targeted evals.
- Metadata returned for each trimmed request listing removed message ids and reasons.
- Ability to enable/disable per-route and per-customer.
- No PII stripping regressions: trimming never removes messages tagged as "sensitive" by the session metadata.

Metrics to track
- Avg tokens/request before vs after trimming.
- Percent of requests trimmed (and by mode).
- End-to-end latency change.
- Quality metrics: BLEU/ROUGE on canned evals + human-rated helpfulness drop.
- Cache hit/eviction change on dedicated pools.
- Customer complaints / support ticket rate about missing context.

Design details / heuristics (notes)
- Age-based: messages older than N minutes are candidate for trimming unless pinned. N default 30m for conservative.
- Redundancy: drop earlier messages with high semantic overlap to later messages (fast sim hash or tiny embedding comparison).
- Role weighting: prefer to keep last user turns + last assistant answers. System messages are protected unless explicitly marked ephemeral.
- Intent-change detection: if a later user message clearly starts a new task, earlier unrelated steps become stronger candidates to trim.
- Length cap: enforce a hard token/window cap; trim oldest candidates first.

API/SDK contract (sketch)
- New request-level param: trimming: {enabled: boolean, mode: "conservative|aggressive|seed-only"} (default off).
- Response has trimming_info: {removed_ids: ["m1","m4"], reasons: ["redundancy","age"], token_delta: "-48"}.
- Console shows a per-route histogram of token_delta and % requests trimmed.

Privacy & Compliance
- Respect session metadata: if session has keep_flags (e.g., "do_not_trim:" [message_ids] or sensitivity label), do not remove.
- Provide an audit export (S3 URI) for customers who request full logs; must follow existing Private controls for Private deployments.

Experiment plan (phase 0/1)
- Phase 0: internal A/B on Canary cluster (internal dataset of long chats). Measure tokens saved and automatic eval quality. Duration 2 weeks.
- Phase 1: enable for 10% of low-risk hosted routes with feedback collection (banner to users or optional preview). 4 weeks.
- Phase 2: ramp with per-customer opt-in and console controls.

Risks / tradeoffs
- Over-trimming could drop crucial context and degrade UX; need conservative defaults and easy rollback.
- Cost to compute trimming decisions (embedding comparisons) could negate savings; prioritize cheap heuristics and cache decisions per session.
- Behavioral differences across models: Llama-like vs. decoder-only might be more sensitive to missing earlier instructions. Need model-aware tuning.

Implementation considerations
- Where to implement: edge filter (fast, per-req) vs control-plane batcher (more informed). Start with edge so it's SDK-visible and per-request.
- Reuse existing embedding endpoints or lightweight L0 text-sim library optimized for short texts (MinHash). Avoid heavy seq2seq summarization in MVP.
- Hook into rollout infra (console) and logs for observability: token delta estimation and a sample of trimmed transcripts for human review (redact PII).

Telemetry and debugging UX
- UI: per-request preview in SDK/devtools: show "kept" vs "removed" with reasons.
- Console: route-level toggle + histogram + list of most common reasons.
- Support: auto-attach trimming_info to request logs to speed triage.

Open questions / TODOs
- Do we expose an API to request an "undo" (re-run inference with full context) on a trimmed request for debugging? Cost implications?
- Exact algorithms for semantic redundancy — do we rely on existing embeddings infra or ship a tiny sim-hash C++ lib in the edge?
- Per-customer policy: should default be off for Private deployments? (likely yes).
- UX language for customers: how to describe "trimming" in a way that doesn't sound like we are deleting their conversation?
- Metrics guardrails: set an alert if human-rated helpfulness drop > 3% or support tickets spike.

Next steps / action items
- Miguel: prototype edge heuristic (age + role + simple text-sim) and run internal benchmark against long-chat corpus. (2 weeks)
- Priya: draft console toggle UX and settings page copy; design an audit export format. (1 week)
- Noah: SRE runbook for safe rollback and knobs for per-customer enforcement in Dedicated/Private. (1 week)
- Lena: coordinate user study for Phase 1 (recruit internal volunteers, design short tasks). (3 weeks)

Notes to self:
- Keep conservative mode on by default.
- Make trimming_info compact and rate-limited in logs.
- Consider a future "compress" mode that replaces clusters of messages with a short summary instead of deleting — follow-up after MVP.

References / inspiration:
- internal: session-presets throttle experiments (see CON-3502)
- academic: "context window management" papers + RL-based selection (too heavy for MVP)

Quick prototype success criteria (internal)
- Average token reduction >= 12% across long-chat dataset and mean human helpfulness delta <= 1.5 points.
- Prototype runs under 15ms overhead per request on edge instance.
